newsitem.title: UK: london Freight - Rates soften in light activity.
newsitem.headline: london Freight - Rates soften in light activity.

text.p: Trading was relatively light and in general rates continued to soften gradually in the London dry cargo freight market.
The Baltic Freight Index reflected this mood shedding nine points to 1,450.
Geared tonnage though, was not affected to any extent and in quiet conditions the Baltic Handy Index rose two points to 1,104.
GRAIN _ Saudi interests were said to be in the process of buying 500,000 tonnes of barley from the Continent, and Glencore was looking for caper tonnage for end April loading to the Mideast Gulf.
Cargill withdrew their enquiry for 2.2/2.8 million cubic feet Brazil/Continent for mid/end April, putting in their own tonnage.
They quoted a new order of 54,000/5 tonnes heavy grain Nopac/Japan for end April/early May though.
Saroc quoted an enquiry for a handy upto panamax size from east coast south America to the Mediterranean for prompt/onwards.
Transcatalana was said to be looking for early replacement tonnage for 50,000 tonnes meals Paranagua/Spanish Mediterranean (last fixed at $14.00).
They were also looking for tonnage for 26/30,000 tonnes soybean meals on this route for May 7/12, while Glencore has an order for 15,000 tonnes sunflower seeds Plate/WC Mexico for April20/25.

The main fixture news concerned Continental's booking of the Andre-relet Royal Ocean for 54,000 tonnes heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Japan for April 15/25 at $24.00 no combo, down 85 cents from Hanjin's fixture of NSAC tonnage on this position a week ago.
Reports circulated that Joy Sea 70,472 dwt was fixed from the U.S. Gulf basis April 20 readiness.
Other talk indicated that 25,000/5 tonnes wheat was fixed St. Lawrence to Algeria for April 15/25 at $23.00.

The Shinwa-relet Maria Bottiglieri 75,265 dwt was thought fixed by Samsun delivery Baltimore mid April (not necessarily for grain) trip Far East at about $14,000/$14,250 daily plus about a $250,000/260,000 ballast bonus, regarded by brokers as not a very generous rate for such business.

Astraguillermo 64,221 dwt was said to have been fixed for an east coast south america round trip, while the Continental-relet Nephele 71,927 dwt was thought to have ballasted from Cigading to the Plate for grain business.
Interbulk was said to have booked a panamax for Brazil/Continent, but in all cases full details were not forthcoming.
News in the smaller sizes was limited to Andre's fixture of 23,500/26,000 tonnes grains 57' prompt Rio Grande do Sul/Poland, possibly at about $26.00.
MINERALS - In a flat caper market, Hoogovens introduced an enquiry for Sepetiba/Muiden ironore for early May shipment, and Yukong 140/160,000 ironore Brazil/Constanza for May 1/15.
In the east, the newbuilding Tian Yang Hai 170,000 dwt was reported fixed on private terms for period business by Navix.
It was also understood that the 1972-built Alina 129,000 dwt failed on subjects with Sinotrans delivery China early May for an Australian round trip at $9,000 daily.
Panamax rates were mixed although generally weaker in the Pacific.

Westernrader 70,329 dwt went to K Line delivery Japan mid April for an east Australian round trip at $12,050 daily and Transworld 71,761 dwt to Navix delivery prompt Taiwan for a trip via west Australia to Japan at close to $12,500 daily.
SE Asia was reported to have proved steadier for owners on Tuesday.
There were reports that Konstantinos A 71,550 dwt was fixed from Indonesia or the Philippines via Australia to Bin Qasim at $12,450 daily.
Elsewhere IMT fixed Glorious Wind 69,000 dwt from Brazil to the U.S. Gulf, and Apollonia Lion 72,044wt was fixed Black Sea/Far East, both on private terms.
At 1505 the BIFFEX futures were five to 15 points easier than Monday's close. Most active May had trade last at 1,490, down five on 25 lots. Total volume traded was 56 lots.
